input.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Sparkling and a reasonableness standard on consent
input.comment: [Playbook] We have added the customary carve-out allowing us to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and a reasonableness standard on consent (with no assignment by Garman to a competitor of ours), since our playbook does not accept a blanket bar on our ability to assign in a corporate reorganisation or M&A transaction. We have also confirmed that Section 3(c) does not cut across this.

ops.oldText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
ops.newText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, provided that (i) Sparkling may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the consent of Garman to any of its affiliates or to any successor by way of merger, amalgamation, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or business, on written notice to Garman, and (ii) Garman may not assign this Agreement to any competitor of Sparkling. No change of control of Sparkling shall constitute an assignment of this Agreement or give rise to any right of Garman to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.

ops.oldText: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
ops.newText: (c) not transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing or as permitted under Section 20(d);
